parts.name: bottle shell

physics.Basic_description: The main body of the bottle, appearing as a matte cream-colored plastic cylinder with a tapered shoulder.
physics.Functional_description: Contains the liquid product and provides the primary structural volume for the container.
physics.Grasped_description: A parallel jaw gripper would grasp the cylindrical mid-section firmly to lift or stabilize the object.
physics.reason: Standard blow-molded plastic bottles are thin-walled shells enclosing air or liquid, not solid blocks of plastic.

parts.description: The main body of the bottle, appearing as a matte cream-colored plastic cylinder with a tapered shoulder.
parts.function: Contains the liquid product and provides the primary structural volume for the container.

parts.name: label band

physics.Basic_description: A tan/brown band wrapped around the center of the bottle body, resembling a paper label or sleeve.
physics.Functional_description: Provides branding, product information, or potentially improved grip friction on the smooth plastic surface.
physics.Grasped_description: Not a primary grasp target; a gripper would contact this surface if grasping the body but relies on the underlying shell for force transmission.
physics.reason: A label is a thin sheet of material that is effectively solid relative to its thickness, lacking an enclosed air cavity in the structural sense.

parts.description: A tan/brown band wrapped around the center of the bottle body, resembling a paper label or sleeve.
parts.function: Provides branding, product information, or potentially improved grip friction on the smooth plastic surface.

parts.name: neck threads

physics.Basic_description: The threaded upper neck of the bottle, visible as a ribbed cream-colored section below the cap area.
physics.Functional_description: Engages with the collar or cap threads to seal the bottle and secure the pump mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Too small and functionally critical to grasp directly; usually avoided to prevent cross-threading or damage.
physics.reason: The neck is a continuation of the hollow bottle shell, requiring an opening for the dip tube and liquid flow.

parts.description: The threaded upper neck of the bottle, visible as a ribbed cream-colored section below the cap area.
parts.function: Engages with the collar or cap threads to seal the bottle and secure the pump mechanism.

parts.name: collar shell

physics.Basic_description: The yellow/orange cylindrical collar at the top, featuring vertical ridges for grip.
physics.Functional_description: Screws onto the bottle neck to hold the pump head assembly in place and allows for tightening/loosening.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper could grasp the knurled sides to rotate the collar for opening or closing the pump lock.
physics.reason: Injection molded screw caps/collars are thin-walled cylinders designed to fit over the bottle neck.

parts.description: The yellow/orange cylindrical collar at the top, featuring vertical ridges for grip.
parts.function: Screws onto the bottle neck to hold the pump head assembly in place and allows for tightening/loosening.

parts.name: collar knurl

physics.Basic_description: The textured, vertically ribbed surface of the yellow collar, designed for high friction.
physics.Functional_description: Increases friction for fingers or grippers to apply torque when screwing the collar on or off.
physics.Grasped_description: Ideal grasp point for rotational manipulation due to the high-friction texture preventing slip.
physics.reason: This is a surface feature of the hollow collar shell, sharing the same thin-wall construction.

parts.description: The textured, vertically ribbed surface of the yellow collar, designed for high friction.
parts.function: Increases friction for fingers or grippers to apply torque when screwing the collar on or off.

parts.name: carrier hub

physics.Basic_description: A small purple/magenta rod-like component visible at the very bottom in the side views, likely the stem or internal hub.
physics.Functional_description: Acts as the central guide or stop for the internal pump spring and piston mechanism.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal or too small to grasp; inaccessible during normal manipulation.
physics.reason: Small internal mechanical components like stems or hubs are typically solid molded plastic to withstand compressive forces.

parts.description: A small purple/magenta rod-like component visible at the very bottom in the side views, likely the stem or internal hub.
parts.function: Acts as the central guide or stop for the internal pump spring and piston mechanism.

parts.name: head shell

physics.Basic_description: The cyan curved spout/nozzle extending from the top, made of smooth light blue plastic.
physics.Functional_description: Directs the dispensed liquid away from the bottle and provides the actuation point for the pump.
physics.Grasped_description: A gripper would press down on the top of this part to actuate the pump, or grasp it to lift the entire assembly if locked.
physics.reason: Pump heads are complex injection molded shells containing internal channels for fluid, but the outer structure is a thin wall.

parts.description: The cyan curved spout/nozzle extending from the top, made of smooth light blue plastic.
parts.function: Directs the dispensed liquid away from the bottle and provides the actuation point for the pump.

parts.name: dip tube

physics.Basic_description: A thin magenta/purple tube extending from the bottom of the assembly (visible in side views as a small protrusion).
physics.Functional_description: Draws liquid from the bottom of the bottle up to the pump mechanism when actuated.
physics.Grasped_description: Internal component (inside the bottle) or too flexible/thin to grasp; not a manipulation handle.
physics.reason: Dip tubes are narrow hollow pipes designed to transport fluid, with very thin walls relative to their length.

simulation.collision: CoACD convex decomposition of concave source collision meshes (relative tolerance 0.03–0.05)
simulation.inertia: Source URDF link inertials; missing inertials use geometry-derived defaults (density 1000 kg/m³)
simulation.friction: Source URDF mu1 as sliding friction; torsional 0.005, rolling 0.0001
simulation.contact: MuJoCo soft contacts (solref 0.01 1); source restitution is displayed, not converted
simulation.material: Rigid bodies; Young’s modulus and Poisson ratio are annotations, not soft-body parameters

interaction.description: Switchable virtual joint damping and reflected armature for interactive inspection; source properties are unchanged.
interaction.rule: damping ≥ rated effort / rated speed; armature = 2% child subtree mass (slide) or 2% mass × collision radius² (hinge)

collisionFilter.description: Self-contact excluded between directly connected rigid groups, including the fixed base; nonadjacent contacts retained
